A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HiFi-Inpaint and contain complete, readable main text, references, and Appendices A–F. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons, component ablations, and a user study in Tables 1–3, plus real-world evaluation in Appendix D and Table 4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental and user-study results, including the real-world evaluation and additional qualitative analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 retain the same data-construction pipeline, high-frequency extraction, token merging, Shared Enhancement Attention, and Detail-Aware Loss. No algorithm, architecture, or training-objective change is reported.

E1.justification: Both use HP-Image-40K and the internal real-world dataset. Appendix F retains the same scenarios involving human-free scenes, full-body views, product interference, and style adaptation.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain Paint-by-Example, ACE++, Insert Anything, and FLUX-Kontext. The comparator subsets in the user study and qualitative comparisons, and the Canny comparison in Figure 3, are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the same metrics, 1024×576 resolution, 1,000-sample synthetic and 2,000-sample real-world test sets, and training settings. The user study still uses 11 image groups and 31 valid responses; Appendix C's baseline input procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The synthetic-data, SEA, and DAL ablations in Table 2 and Figures 6 and 10 are unchanged. Both retain the high-frequency extraction and weighting comparisons in Figures 3–4 and the generalizability analysis in Figure 11.

E5.justification: Both report the same point estimates and averaged preference rates, without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical numerical results and rankings. For example, HiFi-Inpaint's CLIP-I remains 95.0% in Table 1 and 86.8% in Table 4. The qualitative examples and reported findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equations 1–5 retain the same mathematical content, including token definitions, the SEA update, and loss formulations. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions—SEA, DAL, and HP-Image-40K—and the same claims about detail preservation and state-of-the-art performance.

C2.justification: Explanations of baseline failures and component benefits remain unchanged, as do the real-world quality tradeoffs and generalization qualifications in Appendices D–F. No substantive interpretation or limitation is revised.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C retain the same implementation information, including LoRA rank and scaling, padding and resizing, and baseline adaptation prompts. The project-page access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 61 references are unchanged. The paper's positioning relative to existing generation and inpainting methods is retained.

P1.justification: v3 expands the acknowledgments with NSFC Grant 62472403 and thanks to Hao Yang and Ruibiao Lu. It also makes the Implementation Details and Compared Methods headings run into their paragraphs. Scientific prose and section ordering remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Formatting adjustments reflow text across pages 6–10 and shift Table 3 vertically within page 9. Figures, table structures, captions, and appendix layouts remain unchanged; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 adds funding and contributor acknowledgments and makes modest formatting adjustments. Methods, evidence, reproducibility information, claims, and appendices remain unchanged, leaving the paper's overall scientific quality and substantive clarity essentially the same.
